semantic_findings.finding: The sender does not produce process/exited, exitCode, an ACK, process/closed or production state. Existing fake native exit/output notifications remain exact. Both the pre-stage42 and current termination entries already return when their own observer has exited, so requiring another terminate RPC is not a valid server-completion contract.

The channel is sent only after the original non-managed event loop observes TurnComplete. Result checks still require the original success/denial and exact output/code expectations; LegacyExit and ReplayGap still require exactly one read, and Complete/DirectDenied/ElevatedPowerShell retain zero-read assertions. Required compatibility reads must yield their original results before the corresponding output checks can pass.

The original five-second second-model-request observation is moved before server join, retaining the same request count predicate and polling interval. Proxy launch, policy callbacks, remote identity and foreign sandbox assertions remain exact. These branches originally did not independently assert a numeric exit code or compatibility-read count; this patch does not add such coverage, and their pass must not be described as that stronger claim.

Biased select polls the existing RPC reader first. A ready read/terminate uses the untouched handler and unknown methods still panic. Explicit channel success ends only the fixture; sender cancellation is an expect failure, not success. A send failure is ignored only because a server may already have completed its original terminate/patch path; awaiting the original JoinHandle still propagates server panic/error.

The original per-read five-second limit, managed five-second model-output observation and five/fifteen-second join budgets are preserved. Moving the managed observation earlier changes the dependency order without increasing a duration or retry count.

limits: Static-only review; no source edit or Rust/test execution. The native original strict and full Core gates remain required.

The original nine failures identify the generic JSON-RPC read timeout, without a complete RPC transcript. The absence of a server exit path after real native completion is source-proven; the exact failed-loop iteration in each original run is not dynamically captured.

Biased selection protects already-ready requests, not an unbounded drain of messages arriving after fixture completion. The counter is a fixture observation up to the existing model-output/turn boundary, not a proof of no future RPC.
This test-only completion channel must never be reused as production exit evidence or described as an at-most-once kill proof.
